LESSON: COUNTING CONCRETE OBJECTS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Numbers
Topic 2.3: Counting Concrete Objects
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Counting Concrete Objects, part of Numbers in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: How many objects can you see? 2. Why do we use number to match objects you have seen?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Collect in purposive pairs/groups, observe and talk about concrete objects found in school. Learners with manipulative difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or be assisted by peers, learner support assistants or the teacher to collect found objects. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication (AAC) to share their views. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Collect in purposive pairs/groups, observe and talk about concrete objects found in school. Learners with manipulative difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or be assisted by peers, learner support assistants or the teacher to collect found objects. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication (AAC) to share their views. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Counting Concrete Objects together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking and problem solving: learners count and match concrete objects to their corresponding number.

18

Values:
Respect: learners take turns in counting concrete objects 1-20.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Hygiene: learners use concrete objects to count without licking them.

Link to Other Activity Areas:

The learner is able to relate playing counting games to singing games in Creative Activities.
